  3)           You are a data analyst at a fitness app that shows personalized exercise plans to its users.  
  The app has five different workout plans it can recommend as the Plan of the Day: Plan  
  A, Plan B, Plan C, Plan D, and Plan E. When users open the app, they see one of these  
  A)      workout plans, and if they start the workout, it counts as a "success." The objective is to  
  maximize the start rate of workout plans by finding which plan resonates the most with (5)  
  users. However, the performance of each plan is unknown, so you need a strategy to  
  balance exploring different plans to gather data and exploiting the best-performing plan  
  to boost user engagement. Make use of epsilon-greedy algorithm to decide which  
  workout plan to show to users  
  
  B)      Use the above scenario in question 3(a) and write the steps involved in implementation  
  of epsilon-greedy approach.                                                               (5)

  5)              Imagine you are developing a game-playing agent for a board game similar to chess.  
  The agent must learn optimal strategies to win by exploring different moves and their  
  outcomes. To evaluate its performance, you decide to use the Monte Carlo method for  
  A)         policy evaluation. As the agent plays numerous games, it will record the sequence of  
  states, actions, and rewards from each game. After several iterations of playing against  
  itself or other opponents, you want to analyze how the Monte Carlo method can help       (5)  
  improve the agent's policy based on the outcomes of these games. In the context of the  
  board game agent using the Monte Carlo method, Discuss the steps involved in  
  implementing policy evaluation. How does the Monte Carlo method help the agent learn  
  from its experiences, and what are the potential challenges associated with using this  
  approach in dynamic environments?  
  
  B)         Explain the significance of Actor-Critic methods in reinforcement learning and discuss  
  their mechanisms and applications.                                                        (5)
